title: Domain of a Square-Root Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain of g(t)=sqrt(t-3), the set of all real t for which the square root yields a real number.

steps.title: Require the Even Root to Be Nonnegative
steps.explanation: The principal square root sqrt(u) is real only when its radicand u is nonnegative, so we need t-3 >= 0.
steps.why: Even roots of negative numbers are not real, so the radicand condition is the only restriction.

steps.title: Solve the Inequality
steps.explanation: Adding 3 to both sides of t-3 >= 0 gives t >= 3.
steps.why: A linear inequality is solved by isolating the variable.

steps.title: Write the Domain in Interval Form
steps.explanation: The admissible inputs are all t from 3 upward, including 3 itself because sqrt(0)=0 is valid.
steps.why: Bracket at 3 because the endpoint is allowed; the interval is unbounded above.
